idea: Market entry advisory: Chinese cleantech into Europe
buyer: Chinese solar, battery and EV firms expanding into Europe
pain: They do not understand European regulation, buyers or capital
v1: A market entry study for one Chinese manufacturer
verdict: Highest fees in the set and a genuinely warm supply-side channel, but long cycles and payment friction.

why.distribution: Entirely dependent on her father's introductions - the profile caps this at 3 however senior the contacts.
why.demand: Chinese firms are actively spending on European expansion advice.
why.fmf: European capital markets and regulation plus Chinese language and relationships; she lacks trade and customs specifics.
why.defensibility: Trusted bilingual advisors with genuine European credibility are scarce.
why.leverage: Bespoke consulting with heavy relationship management.
why.time_to_revenue: Chinese corporate cycles are long: 6-9 months.
why.tailwind: Chinese cleantech expansion into Europe is a major structural flow, though tariffs are a live risk.
why.ceiling: £35k x 6 engagements = £210k, and six is plausible given the fee size.

ceiling_arithmetic: £35k x 6 engagements = £210k gross, less ~20% for legal and translation = £168k net. Only six clients needed, which makes it reachable; the risk is that year one produces two while relationships build. Realistic: £60-90k.
carries: By far the highest fee per client in the set, needing only six clients, on a genuine structural flow.
kills: Long cycles, real capital outlay before revenue, and total dependence on her father's introductions.
test: Ask her father whether two firms would take a scoping call about European entry.
test_pass: One firm engages for a paid scoping study.
test_fail: Polite meetings that never convert - the common outcome in China business development.
